criteria.text: No change to the observable behavior of the purchase API or of PurchaseService; ADR 0011 and the security invariants continue to hold.
The existing purchase unit, integration, and system tests pass on the candidate.

findings.summary: PurchasePage.of builds nextCursor from fetched.getLast() (the extra limit+1 look-ahead row, which is not returned) instead of the last returned row; with the exclusive (purchased_at, id) < cursor of ADR 0011 / JdbcPurchaseRepository.list, one purchase is silently skipped at every page boundary of GET purchases.
findings.evidence: backend/src/main/java/io/github/stevdrey/dokene/purchase/application/PurchasePage.java:9-11 (boundary = fetched.getLast()) vs base PurchaseService.java:80 (page.getLast()); JdbcPurchaseRepository.java:67 uses an exclusive cursor. Probe runs/K2-pilot/probe/PurchaseListPagingProbeTest.java over 5 purchases, limit=1: candidate pages [p4],[p2],[p0], seen=[p4, p2, p0], test FAILED (runs/K2-pilot/probe-candidate.out); same probe on base 88d7523 sees [p4, p3, p2, p1, p0] for limits 1-3, BUILD SUCCESSFUL (runs/K2-pilot/probe-base.out). Fix: take the cursor from fetched.get(limit - 1), and add a multi-page list test.

findings.summary: No existing purchase test follows a purchase-list nextCursor to a second page, so the AC2 suites pass despite F1; the implementer's no-test rationale for a refactor left this regression undetected.
findings.evidence: PurchaseCurlSystemTest.java:124-126 asserts only that nextCursor is non-blank for limit=1; PurchaseManagementIntegrationTest.java:98-100 pages only revision history.

checks.summary: Identity matches the handoff (tree 897e19fd...). Diff: PurchasePage.java (+of factory), PurchaseService.java (list delegates to it); no untracked files.

checks.environment: disposable copy of the candidate tree plus the probe test file only; JDK 26.0.2; Mockito fakes, the fake repository reproduces the JDBC exclusive cursor and DESC order
checks.summary: Walking all pages via PurchaseService.list with limit=1 returned [p4, p2, p0] instead of all 5 purchases. The same probe passes on base 88d7523 (contrast run, probe-base.out).

checks.environment: disposable copy of the candidate tree; JDK 26.0.2; Testcontainers PostgreSQL
checks.summary: BUILD SUCCESSFUL: PurchaseControllerTest 15, PurchaseTest 2, PurchaseManagementIntegrationTest 5, PurchaseCurlSystemTest 1; 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.

limitations: Checks ran in a disposable copy of the candidate tree (identical backend/src, verified with diff -r) with one extra probe test file, not in the candidate worktree itself.

C1 uses a Mockito fake repository rather than PostgreSQL; the fake mirrors the exclusive cursor of JdbcPurchaseRepository.list and uses distinct timestamps, so the UUID tie-break order is not exercised.
Only the targeted purchase test classes were run (host memory constraint); the full ./gradlew test/check was not run. compileJava claim covered implicitly by C2 compiling on JDK 26.
remainingActions: Fix F1: build nextCursor from the last returned row (fetched.get(limit - 1)), matching the base behavior.
Add a test that follows the purchase-list nextCursor across pages and asserts every purchase appears exactly once (addresses F2), then re-verify.
